title: Common Data Format - Event Data Schema
description:
**Version 0.3.2**

This schema defines the Event Data as described in the [Common Data Format paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.15820).

This schema describes a single JSON Object with a JSON Lines file.

is_synced.description: Indicates if synced tracking data is available (true) or not (false) for this event

time.description: Absolute time in UTC of when the event started (e.g., moment the pass is given, the moment the ball leaves the hands on a thrown in)

period.description: Period of the match which can be first_half, second_half, first_half_extratime, second_half_extratime, or shootout

type.description: Name of the event type (e.g. shot, pass, referee, defending, goalkeeping, misc etc.)

sub_type.description: Name of the event sub type, which can be for shot - (penalty_kick, free_kick, corner_kick etc.); pass - (throw_in, free_kick, corner_kick, goal_kick, kick_off etc.); referee - (final_whistle, foul, caution, offside, substitution, player_on, player_off. Player on and player off events occur for example when a player has to abandon the game due to a lack of available substitutions, or as a temporary measure after a medical check); defending - (clearance, interception, pressing, block etc.); goalkeeping - (save, save_attempt, claim, etc.); misc - (other_ball_action, chance_without_shot, tackle, etc.)

is_successful.description: Denotes whether the event was successful (true) or not (false)

outcome_type.description: Event outcome options: shot - (successful, saved, blocked, wide, woodwork, own_goal); pass - (e.g. successful, out_of_play, intercepted); referee - (start, end, injury, offside, yellow_card, red_card or second_yellow_card); defending - (e.g. clearance, block, interception, pressure); goalkeeping (e.g. save, save_attempt, claim); misc - (e.g. successful, unsuccessful)

player_id.description: Unique identifier of the player performing the action. For example, player committing a pass, or making a tackle. Required for all non-referee events. Referee events require event/official_id.

team_id.description: Unique team identifier of the player performing the action. Required for all non-referee events. Referee events require event/official_id.

official_id.description: Unique identifier of the official performing the action. Mandatory only when type is referee, else use event/player_id and event/team_id

receiver_id.description: Unique identifier of the player receiving a pass. Leave null when the event is not a pass or when the pass has no receiver.

receiver_time.description: Absolute time in UTC of the first moment the ball was received. Leave null when the event is not a pass or when the pass has no receiver.

receiver_team_id.description: Unique team identifier of the player identified by receiver_id, leave null if the event does not end with a known player in possession

x.description: x location where the action of player_id happened (m).

y.description: y location where the action of player_id happened (m).

x_end.description: x location where the action of player_id ended (m), null for single-point events that have no end coordinate.

y_end.description: y location where the action of player_id ended (m), null for single-point events that have no end coordinate.

body_part.description: Denotes the body part used by player_id, null allowed for events other than pass and shot.

related_event_ids.description: Unique identifier(s) of the events related to the action, or pass and associated receival event. For example, a related aerial duel event or the player_off event associated with a player_on event. Leave null if no related events exist.

match_clock.description: The match clock as a string in format "MM:SS.mm" (i.e. minutes, seconds, milliseconds) (e.g. "92:01.04"). The clock resets to "45:00.00", "90:00.00" or "105:00.00" at the start of "second_half", "first_half_extratime", "second_half_extratime", respectively.

reviewed.description: Was this event reviewed by the video assistant referee (true) or not (false)

upheld.description: Was the on-field ruling confirmed (true) or overturned (false)

frame_id.description: Frame identifier from the tracking data related to the event at (x, y)

frame_id_end.description: Frame identifier from the tracking data related to the event at (x_end, y_end)

x.description: x location of the player committing an event according to the tracking data. For example, player committing a pass, or making a tackle (m)

y.description: y location of the player committing an event according to the tracking data. For example, player committing a pass, or making a tackle (m)
